subject: Post-call: Legal/Ops questions on retention, backups, and deletion SLAs

Subject: Post-call recap & a few follow-ups on retention/backups

Hi Julia / Legal Ops team — thanks again for taking the time earlier. Quick recap and a handful of clarifying questions so we can align an MSA-friendly retention approach for PediHealth.

Recap (from our discovery):
- You need HIPAA handling for PHI and vendor controls documented for audits.
- Primary data store retention requested: ability to delete customer data on a 7-30 day SLA depending on record type.
- Logs and backup retention windows are a key sticking point — you need clarity on how deletion propagates to backups.

Questions / asks:
1) SOC 2 / audit artifacts: can you confirm which reports you need (Type I vs Type II) and whether you require a third-party evidence package during procurement?
2) Deletion SLA expectations: you indicated a desire for deletion to be irreversible within 30 days. Can you confirm whether the target is 30 days for primary stores and backups, or 30 days for primary with a longer backup TTL?
3) Backups: are your legal/ops teams ok with backups retained on a schedule (e.g., rolling 90 days) as long as we provide a documented deletion workflow, or do you require immediate backup purge (crypto-erase) tied to key destruction?
4) Immutable backups: do you need WORM/immutable backup retention for specific datasets?
5) KMS / key management: do you require HSM-backed keys for crypto-erase assurances?

Attached: Redwood_Vendor_Security_Questionnaire.pdf (we filled the vendor QA with the items we discussed) and a short technical note describing our retention mechanics (retention-technical-note.md). Please review and return questions or the completed questionnaire from your side.

Next steps I propose:
- Marcus and Laura to provide a short note on Redwood's deletion flow and backup timeline (technical).
- Once Legal Ops confirms target RTO/RPO and backup TTL, we can draft SLA language for the MSA.
- Schedule 30-minute follow-up on Thu to walk through the questionnaire and any redlines.

Can you confirm availability for Thu 9/9 9–11am PT?

Thanks — Priya

Hi Priya — thanks for the clear notes. A few quick answers from our side before the call: 

- SOC 2: we need the Type II report and a list of controls mapped to HIPAA (if you can provide a control matrix that would be ideal).
- HIPAA: yes, covered. We need BAAs in place and evidence of encryption at rest and in transit.
- Deletion SLA: our legal baseline asks for deletion from primary store within 7 days of request, and confirmation that backups will not retain recoverable copies past 30 days. We are amenable to a documented workflow where backups are retained a bit longer but immutable snapshots containing PHI must be addressable for purge or crypto-erase.
- Backups: we prefer a crypto-erase option for faster irreversibility; if that is not possible, we need a contract clause that ties backup retention to a maximum of 30 days for PHI.
- KMS: we prefer HSM-backed keys and customer-managed keys if possible.

I attached our internal spec for data retention so you can see the exact language our legal team will push (PediHealth_Data_Retention_Reqs.pdf).

We can do Thu 9/9 10am PT. Please send an invite.

Thanks,
Julia

Hi Julia — quick technical replies to the items you listed, to help Legal Ops evaluate tradeoffs before the call.

1) Deletion flow (high level):
- Soft delete: user/agent triggers delete -> data marked for deletion and becomes immediately inaccessible via the API.
- Purge: background job runs to permanently delete primary-store objects within configurable window (typically 24–168 hours depending on tenant settings).
- Backups: snapshots are managed by our backup scheduler. By default backups are retained as rolling snapshots for 90 days. Purge of a primary object does not automatically rewrite historical snapshot files until the snapshot window that includes the deleted object rolls out.

2) Options we can offer to meet a 30-day backup horizon for PHI:
- Crypto-erase: rotate and destroy the encryption key for the tenant (HSM-backed option available under Private deployment / enterprise contract). This renders backup ciphertext unrecoverable immediately.
- Fast-retention policy: configure backup retention to a maximum of 30 days for datasets flagged as PHI. This requires coordination on snapshot granularity and may incur additional operational verification steps.
- Immutable snapshots with exclusion rules: we can provide immutable backups for certain datasets while ensuring PHI-containing snapshots are tagged for shorter retention.

3) KMS: we support provider-managed keys by default and customer-managed keys (CMK) with HSM-backed stores on Dedicated/Private tiers. We can document key lifecycle and crypto-erase procedures for contract language.

4) Evidence / artifacts: we can share our SOC 2 Type II report and a control mapping for HIPAA in a redacted package. Our SOC 2 audit is completed and artifacts are available under NDA / secure link.

Next steps from our side: Laura will prepare a one-page SLA paragraph describing deletion timing (soft-delete -> purge windows) and backup options. We'll also produce a short appendix that describes crypto-erase and CMK workflows so Legal can evaluate.
